intended_object: Given closed subgroups N, H of a profinite group G and an open normal subgroup U, this is the relative index [π_U(H) : π_U(N) ∩ π_U(H)] of the images of N and H in the finite quotient G/U, viewed as a supernatural number. When N ≤ H this is the U-stage of the profinite index [H : N]. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `finiteQuotientIndex_tower` and `finiteQuotientIndex_within_eq_relIndex`.
explanation:
The body takes the images of N and H under `QuotientGroup.mk' U` and returns Mathlib's `Subgroup.relIndex` of the first in the second. By Mathlib's convention, `A.relIndex B` is the index of A ⊓ B in B. So the result is [H̄ : N̄ ∩ H̄], and when N ≤ H it is [H̄ : N̄], the usual finite-stage relative index.

G/U is finite, so the image of N has finite index and the relative index is a positive natural number. Wrapping it with `ofPNat` into the supernatural numbers is therefore correct. There are no hidden junk values, because positivity is proved from `isFiniteRelIndex_of_finiteIndex`.

The library's lemmas confirm this reading:
- `finiteQuotientIndex_tower` proves [G/U : N̄] = [G/U : H̄]·(this quantity) when N ≤ H.
- `finiteQuotientIndex_within_eq_relIndex` identifies it with the finite-stage index of N inside H.

The definition is the finite-quotient stage of profinite indices and is stated in its natural setting: closed subgroups of a profinite group and open normal subgroups. It is admittedly mostly a building block for the tower law. Mathlib has no supernatural-valued counterpart.
